answer: Registration cost is where a sybil swarm dies. Every new identity must post bond into a commitment kernel that escrows real value for a fixed term, so forging a thousand puppets bills a thousand bonds and a farm's bill rises with its headcount instead of staying flat. When they collude, peers slash each bond, so the attacker pays per seat rather than per campaign. The relic of past bond slashed per address stays readable across epochs, so a fresh tenure cannot reset the record. A bond also acts as a bridge: vouching for a stranger stakes your standing, and a false attestation burns it.
